test_title: PYST 43: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 16 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: One pipe can fill a tank in 8 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 16 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Filling rate = 1/8, Emptying rate = 1/16

Net rate = 1/8 − 1/16 = 1/16

Time for full tank = 16 minutes

Time for half tank = 16 ÷ 2

**∴ Answer = 8 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Filling pipe fills tank in 8 minutes, emptying pipe empties tank in 16 minutes

**Formula used:**

Net work = Filling rate − Emptying rate

**Calculation:**

⇒ Filling rate = 1/8 tank per minute

⇒ Emptying rate = 1/16 tank per minute

⇒ Net rate = 1/8 − 1/16

⇒ = 2/16 − 1/16 = 1/16 tank per minute

⇒ Time to fill full tank = 1 ÷ (1/16) = 16 minutes

⇒ Time to fill half tank = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

Filling is positive work and emptying is negative work

Net Rate

Net rate = Sum of individual rates (consider signs)

Time Formula

Time = Work ÷ Rate

Shortcut Insight

If net rate is constant, half work takes half time
